Subject: Sizing for dedicated pool — context and quantization questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're moving toward a committed Redwood Dedicated pilot and need more concrete sizing guidance before procurement. A couple of specifics we want to validate:

- Our primary model is a 70B-class decoder (open-llm-64k variant) with a 64k context window for retrieval-augmented generation. Typical interactive sessions average ~18–35k tokens (user + assistant + retrieval).
- Target sustained concurrency for the pilot: 12 active sessions (peak concurrency expected 18), with occasional batch workloads (up to 40 concurrent short requests).
- Hard SLAs: 95th pct latency target of <700ms for single-turn generation (100–300 tokens), and retention of KV cache for session-based workflows.

Questions:
1) How much GPU memory headroom does KV caching for 64k contexts consume per session for a 70B model, and what does that imply for per-GPU concurrent session capacity?
2) How much reduction can we expect from 4-bit quantization (Q4/KH-type) on model weights and KV storage? Any notes on trade-offs for latency or quality?
3) If we rely on KV offload to host memory for long contexts, what are the CPU/network trade-offs we should expect?

I'm attaching our short SLO/usage sheet. Can you push a preliminary sizing workbook back with ballpark GPU counts and RAM assumptions? We'd like to loop procurement by end of next week.

Best,
Evan

Hi Evan — thanks, and appreciate the detail. Attaching an initial sizing workbook (emberlane_initial_sizing.xlsx) and a short readout. High level answers up front, then a few assumptions we used:

Quick answers:
- KV headroom: for the 70B-class model at 64k context we estimate ~18–28 GB of KV storage per active session in our conservative FP16 path (depends on layer/hidden-size specifics).
- Quantization: moving to Q4-style weight quant reduces model parameter memory by ~45–55% (weights only). KV cache reduction from quantizing activations/KV is more modest (~10–25%) unless using KV-specific packing; biggest wins come from offload and more aggressive KV compression.
- Offload: KV offload to host RAM lowers GPU RAM requirements but adds CPU and PCIe/host-NIC bandwidth pressure; expect 15–40ms additional tail latency for cache fetches unless using NVMe-backed pinned regions and optimized pinning strategies.

Ballpark concurrency examples (derived in workbook):
- Conservative (FP16 weights, no KV offload): 12 active sessions at median 25k tokens -> ~6x A100-80GB GPUs for baseline throughput and headroom.
- Aggressive (Q4 weights + KV offload with per-session compression): same workload -> ~3x GPUs (but higher CPU/NIC utilization and more operational complexity).

Assumptions used in workbook: model architecture analogous to 70B decoder, KV per-token cell size ~420 bytes (includes key+value packed with layer count assumptions), average effective context per active session 25k tokens, target steady-state margin 20% for spikes.

Next steps:
1) Marcus — please review the KV per-token estimate and add a short note on offload latency profile.
2) Karthik — can you confirm whether canary fallback model (smaller 13B low-latency variant) is feasible from product-side for SLA-preserving fallbacks?
3) Evan/Amrita — can we set a 60-minute call Thurs to walk through the workbook and finalize procurement targets?

Thanks — sending the workbook now.

Cheers,
Priyom Das

On Thu, Jul 15, 2028 at 12:38 PM priyom_das@redwood.ai wrote:
> Attaching an initial sizing workbook...

Following up with more engineering detail and conservative/calibrated numbers so procurement has defensible targets. I'm copying the quick math here so it's explicit in-thread.

Engineer's notes / assumptions (conservative):
- Model family: 70B decoder, 40 layers, hidden dim ~7k (approx). KV entries per token ~2 matrices (K and V), K/V vector size ~3584 bytes combined across heads/layers when packed in FP16 (we round to estimate). This yields ~0.38–0.45 KB per token in packed FP16 per layer aggregate; across 40 layers that produces the workbook's per-token KV footprint.
- Workbook used ~420 bytes/token aggregate (FP16 packed across layers) -> 64k context => ~26.9 GB KV per session. For 25k average context -> ~10.5 GB/session.

GPU capacity planning examples (we recommend sizing by steady-state + burst headroom):
- Scenario A (FP16, no offload): target 12 steady sessions at median 25k -> total KV RAM ~126 GB plus model weights ~75 GB (FP16), working memory, and OS overhead -> target fleet: 6x A100-80GB (with reserved headroom for spiky bursts).
- Scenario B (Q4 weights, partial KV quant + offload): weights down to ~34 GB, KV per-session lowered via compression to ~8 GB (avg), plus offload tradeoffs. Same concurrency fits on 3x A100-80GB; requires pinned host RAM and higher NIC throughput (we measured ~6–8 GB/s sustained for 12 sessions during internal tests).

Operational caveats:
- KV offload reduces capex but increases operational risk: PCIe/NIC saturation, GC pauses if host memory ballooning, and slightly higher 95/99 tail latencies.
- We should test end-to-end with Emberlane's 64k retrieval traces; synthetic assumptions can be off by ±20–30% depending on tokenization and prefix ratios.

I'll add recommended monitoring signals into the workbook (KV growth per session, NVMe read latencies, NIC utilization, model quantization regression tests).

— Marcus Lin
